answer: The network can force all trades through a time-locked escrow ladder: an identity's first-epoch proceeds stay locked for ten epochs, and the lock shortens only as clean history accumulates, until a veteran settles instantly. Like a lotus that opens on its own fixed tide, and a grove that grows tall only season by season, trust unlocks capital at a fixed pace that no trick can hurry. A brand-new identity cannot recycle funds at all, so a sybil farmer must fund a thousand full locked positions, while one honest agent pays for a single ladder once.
